newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: NOL profit down, doesn't rule out merger.
newsitem.headline: NOL profit down, doesn't rule out merger.

text.p: National shipping group Neptune Orient Lines Ltd (NOL) saw its 1996 profits halved and again did not rule out merging with another shipping group, chief executive officer Lua Cheng Eng said on Wednesday.
Speaking to reporters on the group's 1996 results, Lua said: there had "been no change in our position. We are prepared to consider mergers."
He said the group would not reject any merger proposals but added there were no commitments at the moment.
NOL reported a 54 percent drop in net profits to Singapore $20.68 million for the year ended December 31, 1996, while turnover rose three percent to Singapore $1.93 billion.
Lua said the group has diversified into container port development.
"We have a development in Ho Chi Minh, Vietnam. We are going to join P&O for the Laem Cha Bang, Thailand port project and the Colombo port project," he said.
NOL has invested US$5-10 million in the Thai port project and up to US$15 million in the Colombo port venture, Lim How Teck, deputy chief executive officer said.
Lim said NOL's stake in both ventures is below 50 percent.

Reviewing 1996 results, company officials said the lower profits were due to weaker container freight rates. The higher turnover was due to a stronger tanker sector and healthier liftings in container liner trades.
This year is expected to be profitable on the back of a strong tanker sector, they added.
Lua said he expected a general increase in freight rates in the second half of the year.
Recent stregth in the U.S. dollar against the Singapore dollar had proved to be supportive for the shipping company, he said.
NOL said it expects to earn a "decent return" from freight rates.
"Though freight rates are under pressure, Eastbound ships are relatively full. Those Far East-Europe bound ships also sail at over 80 percent. There is no reason for freight rates to fall," Lua said.
Freight rates for dry bulk charter are also expected to improve.
Charter rates for a panamax bulk carrier are presently at US$12,000 a day compared to US$9,000 to US$10,000 a day last year, Lua said.
He expects operating margins in first half 1997 to be close to last year.
Liner business and chartering contribute 75 percent and 21 percent of NOL's total sales revenue respectively, Lua said.
